item.title: Fin de la misión de la ONU en el Sahara Occidental: una meta incumplida y un futuro incierto

item.title: Negotiators ‘braced for worst’ over US-Iran talks to reopen strait of Hormuz
item.description: Third day of indirect talks as Qatar tries to negotiate release of $6bn in Iranian assets that could lead to waterway’s reopening Officials from the Gulf states are “braced for the worst” as they wait for Washington’s response to an Iranian proposal that could reopen the strait of Hormuz before the US midterm elections on Tuesday. Indirect talks in Doha ran into a third day on Sunday with Qatar trying to negotiate the release of more than $6bn in Iranian assets, which could lead to the reopening of the strait of Hormuz and the restart of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme. item.title: Trump says Bolsonaro can remain in US indefinitely, calls Brazil election a 'disgrace'
item.description: Flavio Bolsonaro left Brazil after his electoral defeat, despite having led in several opinion polls. His departure came after a Brazilian Supreme Court justice ordered his passport revoked. He is also facing two federal money-laundering investigations, while police in Brazil had considered him a flight risk. item.title: Ecuador inicia su cuarto toque de queda del año para contener la violencia a semanas de las elecciones locales
item.description: El país inició este domingo 1 de noviembre su cuarto período de restricciones nocturnas de movilidad en lo corrido del año. Se trata de una medida que regirá durante diez días en cinco provincias de la costa, entre ellas Guayas, donde se encuentra Guayaquil, la ciudad más poblada de Ecuador. El nuevo toque de queda llega en medio de una persistente crisis de seguridad, marcada por la expansión de las organizaciones criminales y el narcotráfico, y a cuatro semanas de unas elecciones locales en las que la seguridad vuelve a ocupar un lugar central en la disputa política. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.description: Chancellor John Healey fails to guarantee equalisation with adult wage will happen in timeframe set out in manifesto Labour looks less likely to meet its manifesto pledge to equalise the minimum wage for younger workers before the next election, after the chancellor failed to guarantee the rise would happen within that timeframe.
